alignments.note: Fixed interrogative idiom 'διὰ τί' rendered by the single word 'Why'; neither the preposition nor the interrogative is separately recoverable. Head on the interrogative, as at 8:46 and JHN.7.45. Splitting it as an unrepresented preposition plus 'Why' on the interrogative remains defensible.
The possessive emen occupies the English determiner slot ('my speech'), so the article realizes nothing.
Second attributive article with no English realization.
Inflected verb takes its English auxiliary and subject; head is the lexical verb.
The supplied 'Even' intensifies the conjunction it introduces and is treated as its helper rather than 'added'; taking it as 'added' remains defensible.
The ASV spells the negation into the modal ('cannot'), so negative and verb form one unit; 'ye' is the verb's subject helper.
The possessive emon occupies the English determiner slot ('my word'), so the article realizes nothing.
